claims.text: The multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy develops stable protective oxide films under static high-temperature conditions.
The alloy has intact heterogeneous phase boundaries in its initial state.
Heterogeneous phase boundaries act as preferential corrosion sites.
Mechanical wear disrupts the protective high-temperature oxide scale.
Disruption of the oxide scale exposes fresh alloy substrate.
Freshly exposed substrate corrodes more rapidly than oxide-covered substrate.
Preferential corrosion of interphase boundaries embrittles the alloy structure.
Corrosion-induced embrittlement increases subsequent wear damage.
The feedback between oxide removal, corrosion, boundary embrittlement, and wear accelerates overall degradation.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion produce greater total degradation than either wear-only or corrosion-only exposure at the same temperature.
The wear response is increased under simultaneous wear and corrosion relative to a wear-only baseline.
The corrosion response is increased under simultaneous wear and corrosion relative to a corrosion-only baseline.
Protective oxide films remain more intact during single-mode exposure than during simultaneous wear and corrosion.
Phase boundaries are less compromised during single-mode exposure than during simultaneous wear and corrosion.
The proposed synergy requires a temperature high enough to sustain relevant oxidation and corrosion kinetics.
The proposed synergy requires mechanical wear energetic enough to disrupt the oxide scale.
Outside the stated thermal and mechanical regimes, the degradation synergy may not occur.

contradictions.description: The controls are defined as wear-only and corrosion-only, but the design also requires identical loading and atmosphere conditions for all groups. A corrosion-only control cannot receive the same wear-producing mechanical loading, and a wear-only control generally cannot receive the same corrosive atmosphere, without ceasing to be a single-mode control.
